summary.en-US: Understand extension permissions and review meaningful changes without sending browser data anywhere.

release_notes.en-US: Corrects how website access is rated. An add-on that can reach every site over a single scheme, such as https, is now reported as having access to every website instead of appearing limited, and access to one specific site is no longer overstated. Permissions that Extension Watchdog does not recognize now ask you to review them rather than being left out of the summary. The dashboard also refreshes an out-of-date snapshot when you open it. Extension Watchdog's own permissions, data practices, and local-only behavior are unchanged.

version.approval_notes:
Version 0.1.2 corrects two classification defects found in a security review and adds a snapshot freshness window.

Host permissions were matched by string shape, so a wildcard host carrying a specific scheme was missed: "https://*/*" returned false from both the all-sites and the broad-access checks and could receive the default limited rating. Match patterns are now parsed structurally in extension/background/classifier.js. A wildcard host counts as every host regardless of scheme, a wildcard subdomain counts as broad, and a single host stays narrow even when its scheme is wildcarded, which also stops "*://example.com/*" from being overstated. The dashboard held a second copy of the same test and now reads the classifier's recorded finding instead.

Permissions absent from the bundled rules file previously produced no finding at all, so an unrecognized capability disappeared from the summary and left an add-on looking limited. Unknown API permissions and unparseable host patterns now produce an explicit review-required finding, and extension/rules/permissions.json was expanded to the documented Firefox permission catalog so the fallback only applies to genuinely unreviewed capabilities.

Firefox does not raise a management event when a user grants or revokes an optional permission, so a stored snapshot could stay stale until a manual scan or a restart. Snapshots are now trusted for five minutes and a stale one is refreshed the next time the popup or dashboard requests state. This is triggered by user interaction; no background polling loop was added and scan operations remain serialized.

The requested permissions are unchanged at management, storage, and notifications. There are still no host permissions and no content scripts. No network behavior, telemetry, or remote service was introduced, all extension-supplied strings are rendered with textContent, and declared data collection remains none. Dependencies are now installed from a committed lockfile with npm ci, and release workflow actions are pinned to full commit SHAs. Tests pass: 12 static checks and 14 classifier regressions. Mozilla lint reports 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 notices.
